To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) innocent people can generate alibis, but a substantial proportion are mistaken; (2) the quality of alibis decreases over time; and (3) innocent alibi providers often fail to corroborate alibis with strong evidence.
innocent alibi generators may be unable to produce convincing alibis, especially for events in the distant past.

(1) innocent suspects may have difficulty generating alibis that are convincing to evaluators; (2) innocent suspects’ alibis are likely to be mistaken; (3) the accuracy of innocent suspects’ alibi narratives decreases with time; and (4) innocent suspects may be more likely to generate alibis that contain weak evidence than strong evidence.

the quality of innocent people’s alibis.

the quality of alibis, the factors that influence the quality of alibi generation, and the implications of these factors for the legal system.
